children.title: Direct Sums
children.top_down_role: Composition of matroids on disjoint ground sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct sum of finite matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_1=(E_1,\mathcal I_1)\) and \(M_2=(E_2,\mathcal I_2)\) be finite matroids with \(E_1\cap E_2=\varnothing\). Their direct sum \(M_1\oplus M_2\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) with
\[\mathcal I(M_1\oplus M_2)=\{I_1\cup I_2:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}.\]
Equivalently, for every \(X\subseteq E_1\cup E_2\),
\[r_{M_1\oplus M_2}(X)=r_{M_1}(X\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(X\cap E_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum combines disjoint matroids independently, so independent sets and ranks decompose componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M_1\oplus M_2)=\{I_1\cup I_2:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}\).

notation.meaning: direct sum of the two matroids
independent-set family of the ith matroid
rank function of the ith matroid

children.title: Two-Sums
children.top_down_role: Composition through a shared interface element followed by its removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit definition of the binary gluing operation along one ordinary element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i\) be finite matroids on \(E_i\) with \(E_1\cap E_2=\{p\}\), where \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either matroid. The two-sum \(M_1\oplus_2 M_2\) has ground set \((E_1\cup E_2)\setminus\{p\}\). Its circuits are the circuits of each \(M_i\) avoiding \(p\), together with all sets
\[(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\},\]
where \(C_i\) is a circuit of \(M_i\) containing \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sum glues two matroids along one nonloop, noncoloop element and then removes it, joining circuits that used the shared element.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either \(M_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C(M_1\oplus_2M_2)=\mathcal C_1^{\neg p}\cup\mathcal C_2^{\neg p}\cup\{(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\}:p\in C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i)\}\).

notation.meaning: circuits of the ith matroid avoiding p

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Sum Connectivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Connectivity distinctions separating direct-sum and two-sum decompositions.

assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are finite matroids with \(E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=\{p\}\).
\(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either matroid.
For the connectivity assertion, both \(M_i\) are connected and \(|E(M_i)|\ge 3\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct sums realize the disconnected regime, whereas the two-sum \(M_1\oplus_2 M_2\) is connected under the stated hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite direct-sum and two-sum connectivity regimes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M\), a partition \(E(M)=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}Y\) is a direct-sum separation exactly when \(\lambda_M(X)=0\), equivalently \(M=M|X\oplus M|Y\). If \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) satisfy the assumptions, their two-sum has ground set \((E(M_1)\cup E(M_2))\setminus\{p\}\) and bases \((B_1\cup B_2)\setminus\{p\}\), where each \(B_i\) is a basis of \(M_i\) and exactly one of \(B_1,B_2\) contains \(p\). The resulting two-sum is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct sums are exactly zero-connectivity separations. Gluing two connected matroids across a common nonloop, noncoloop and then deleting it produces a connected two-sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Sum Connectivity Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Parallel Connections
children.top_down_role: Matroid composition through a common basepoint.

assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are finite matroids on \(E_1,E_2\) with \(E_1\cap E_2=\{p\}\).
\(p\) is not a loop of either matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed circuit family determines the parallel connection \(P(M_1,M_2)\) and restricts to \(M_i\) on each \(E_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit definition for a one-element interface.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The parallel connection \(P(M_1,M_2)\) with basepoint \(p\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) whose circuits are the inclusion-minimal nonempty members of \[\mathcal C(M_1)\cup\mathcal C(M_2)\cup\{(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\}: C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i),\ p\in C_1\cap C_2\}.\] In particular, \(P(M_1,M_2)|E_i=M_i\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\), and the common element \(p\) remains in the ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parallel connection retains both matroids and adds circuits formed by joining one circuit from each side through their common nonloop basepoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Connections

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Generalized Parallel Connections
children.top_down_role: Matroid composition across a larger shared restriction.

assumptions_latex: \(M_i\) is a finite matroid on \(E_i\), \(T=E_1\cap E_2\), and \(M_1|T=M_2|T=N\).
\(T\) is a modular semiflat of at least one of \(M_1,M_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum formula defines the generalized parallel connection \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\), an amalgam restricting to both input matroids.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proper-amalgam rank representation under a modular-semiflat interface.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(T\) is a modular semiflat of \(M_1\) when \(\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\) is modular and every element of \(\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\) is in \(T\), is a loop, or is parallel to an element of \(T\). Under the assumptions, the generalized parallel connection \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) with rank \[r_P(X)=\min_{Y:\,X\subseteq Y\subseteq E_1\cup E_2}\bigl(r_{M_1}(Y\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(Y\cap E_2)-r_N(Y\cap T)\bigr).\] It satisfies \(P|E_i=M_i\) for \(i=1,2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible matroids can be amalgamated across a modular-semiflat common restriction; the proper-amalgam minimum formula gives the resulting rank function.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Parallel Connections

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Connection Interface Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions on shared restrictions supporting connection constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Agreement on \(T\) is necessary; a modular-semiflat interface is sufficient for the canonical proper amalgam, while arbitrary compatible interfaces need not admit one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary compatibility and standard sufficient interface condition.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An amalgam \(P\) on \(E(M_1)\cup E(M_2)\) satisfying \(P|E(M_i)=M_i\) can exist only if the two restrictions to the overlap agree: \(M_1|T=M_2|T\). Agreement alone does not guarantee existence or uniqueness. A standard sufficient regime is that \(T\) be a modular semiflat of at least one input matroid; then the proper-amalgam rank formula defines the canonical generalized parallel connection \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\). Thus interface compatibility is necessary, while modular-semiflat structure supplies the additional rank consistency needed by this construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inputs must agree on their overlap. A modular-semiflat overlap guarantees the canonical generalized parallel connection; mere agreement may not guarantee any amalgam or uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Connection Interface Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Parallel-Connection Specialization
children.top_down_role: Placement of ordinary parallel connection within the generalized construction.

assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are finite matroids, \(E_i=E(M_i)\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\), and \(E_1\cap E_2=\{p\}\).
\(p\) is not a loop of either matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized parallel connection over \(N=U_{1,1}\) equals the ordinary parallel connection: \(P_N(M_1,M_2)=P(M_1,M_2)\).

notation.meaning: Ground set of the input matroid M_i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singleton-interface specialization of generalized parallel connection.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Both restrictions to \(\{p\}\) equal \(N=U_{1,1}\), and the singleton interface is a modular semiflat. For every \(X\subseteq E_1\cup E_2\), the generalized parallel connection has rank \[r_{P_N(M_1,M_2)}(X)=\min_{Y:\,X\subseteq Y\subseteq E_1\cup E_2}\bigl(r_{M_1}(Y\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(Y\cap E_2)-r_N(Y\cap\{p\})\bigr).\] The matroid defined by this specialization is the ordinary parallel connection, so \(P_N(M_1,M_2)=P(M_1,M_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the common restriction is one nonloop element, the generalized parallel-connection rank formula specializes exactly to the ordinary parallel connection.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Connection Specialization

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Single-Element Extensions
children.top_down_role: Matroid enlargement by one new element.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single-element extension is exactly a matroid \(M'\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) satisfying \(M'\setminus e=M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite single-element extension, including loop and coloop cases.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-element extension of \(M\) by \(e\) is a matroid \(M'\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) such that \(M'\setminus e=M\). Equivalently, \(r_{M'}(X)=r_M(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\), while for each \(X\subseteq E\), \(r_{M'}(X\cup\{e\})\) is either \(r_M(X)\) or \(r_M(X)+1\), consistently with the matroid rank axioms. The extension is a loop extension when \(e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M'}(\varnothing)\) and a coloop extension when \(r(M')=r(M)+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-element extension adds one element whose deletion recovers the original matroid; its rank contribution over each old subset is zero or one.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Element Extensions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Single-Element Coextensions
children.top_down_role: Dual enlargement associated with single-element extensions.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single-element coextension is exactly a matroid \(N\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) satisfying \(N/e=M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite coextension defined through contraction and dual extension.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-element coextension of \(M\) by \(e\) is a matroid \(N\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) such that \(N/e=M\). Equivalently, duality converts the construction into an extension: \(N\) is a coextension of \(M\) if and only if \(N^*\setminus e=M^*\). Thus cocircuits and corank behavior of a coextension are obtained by applying the circuit and rank description of a single-element extension to the dual matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coextension adds one element whose contraction recovers the original matroid; equivalently, its dual is a single-element extension of the dual matroid.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Element Coextensions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Modular-Cut Encoding
children.top_down_role: Encoding of extension choices through modular cuts in the flat lattice.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Modular cuts of \(M\) are in bijection with single-element extensions of \(M\) on a fixed new element.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical modular-cut encoding of finite one-element extensions.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A modular cut is a collection \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal F(M)\) that is upward closed among flats and satisfies: if \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal C\) and \(r(F_1)+r(F_2)=r(F_1\cap F_2)+r(F_1\cup F_2)\), then \(F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal C\). For an extension \(M'\) by \(e\), its cut is \(\mathcal C_e=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M'}(F)\}\). Conversely, \(\mathcal C\) determines the extension through \[r_{M'}(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal C,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal C.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modular cut records exactly which old flats span the new element, and this data uniquely determines the single-element extension rank function.
knowledge_statements.title: Modular-Cut Encoding

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Extension–Coextension Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between extension and coextension regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\setminus e=M\) if and only if \(N^*/e=M^*\), and \(N/e=M\) if and only if \(N^*\setminus e=M^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion–contraction duality for one-element constructions.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matroid duality exchanges deletion and contraction: \((N\setminus e)^*=N^*/e\) and \((N/e)^*=N^*\setminus e\). Consequently, \(N\) is a single-element extension of \(M\) exactly when \(N^*\) is a single-element coextension of \(M^*\), and \(N\) is a single-element coextension of \(M\) exactly when \(N^*\) is a single-element extension of \(M^*\). The correspondence is involutive because \((M^*)^*=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges single-element extensions with coextensions because it exchanges deletion with contraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Extension–Coextension Duality

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

children.title: Extension Realizability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on admissible extension data.

assumptions_latex: \(A=(a_x)_{x\in E}\) represents \(M\) over a field \(\mathbb F\) in a vector space \(V\).
\(W\) is a vector space containing \(V\), and \(v\in W\) represents a proposed new element \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An extension preserving the fixed representation is realizable exactly when its modular cut equals \(\{F:v\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F}\{a_x:x\in F\}\}\) for some \(W\supseteq V\) and \(v\in W\).

notation.meaning: Linear span over the representation field

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability relative to a fixed linear representation and field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Appending \(v\) to \(A\) produces a represented extension whose modular cut is \[\mathcal C_v=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):v\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F}\{a_x:x\in F\}\}.\] Conversely, every extension that extends this fixed representation arises from such a vector in some ambient \(W\supseteq V\). Therefore an abstract modular cut need not be realizable over \(\mathbb F\) relative to \(A\): realizability fails precisely when no vector has the prescribed incidences with the spans of all flats. Allowing \(v\notin V\) includes the coloop extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed linear representation, realizable extensions are exactly modular cuts induced by one vector’s membership in flat spans; other modular cuts are unrealizable there.
knowledge_statements.title: Extension Realizability Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Matroid Quotients
children.top_down_role: Strong-map quotient relationships between matroids.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(Q\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) exactly when every flat of \(Q\) is a flat of \(M\).

notation.meaning: Deletion and contraction of an auxiliary set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-map definition and common-minor characterization of finite quotients.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) when the identity map on \(E\) is a strong map from \(M\) to \(Q\), equivalently when \(\mathcal F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal F(M)\). For finite matroids this is also equivalent to the existence of a matroid \(L\) on \(E\mathbin{\dot\cup}X\), for some finite auxiliary set \(X\), such that \(M=L\setminus X\) and \(Q=L/X\). Thus contraction of the auxiliary elements modifies rank while retaining the same displayed ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient has no flats beyond those of the original matroid; equivalently, both arise as deletion and contraction of the same auxiliary elements.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Quotients

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Matroid Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lift relationships dual to quotient structure.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(L\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is a lift of \(M\) exactly when \(M\) is a quotient of \(L\), equivalently when \(L^*\) is a quotient of \(M^*\).

notation.meaning: Deletion and contraction of auxiliary elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite lifts as reverse quotients, with dual characterization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(L\) is a lift of \(M\) if \(M\) is a quotient of \(L\). Equivalently, there exist a finite set \(X\) disjoint from \(E\) and a matroid \(K\) on \(E\mathbin{\dot\cup}X\) such that \(L=K\setminus X\) and \(M=K/X\). By deletion–contraction duality, this holds if and only if \(L^*\) is a quotient of \(M^*\). In flat language, the quotient relation gives \(\mathcal F(M)\subseteq\mathcal F(L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift reverses the quotient relation: deleting auxiliary elements gives the lift, while contracting them gives the original matroid; duality converts lifts back to quotients.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Lifts

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Matroid Truncations
children.top_down_role: Rank-lowering construction preserving lower-cardinality independence.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Truncations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rank truncation of a finite matroid by an integer threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid with rank function \(r_M\), and let \(k\) satisfy \(0\le k\le r_M(E)\). The rank-\(k\) truncation \(T_k(M)\) is the matroid on \(E\) whose independent sets and rank function are
\[\mathcal I(T_k(M))=\{I\in\mathcal I:|I|\le k\},\qquad r_{T_k(M)}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),k\}\quad(X\subseteq E).\]
Its bases are exactly the independent \(k\)-subsets of \(M\). The ordinary truncation is \(T_{r_M(E)-1}(M)\) when \(r_M(E)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncation caps every set's rank at k; its independent sets are precisely the original independent sets having at most k elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{T_k(M)}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),k\}\) for every \(X\subseteq E\).

source_refs.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

children.title: Free Extensions
children.top_down_role: Generic single-element extension regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Free Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the one-element free extension, including the rank-zero convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid of rank \(r\), and let \(e\notin E\). The free extension \(M+e\) is the matroid on \(E\cup\{e\}\) with independent sets
\[\mathcal I(M+e)=\mathcal I\cup\{J\cup\{e\}:J\in\mathcal I,\ |J|<r\}.\]
Thus deletion of \(e\) returns \(M\), while \(e\) lies in the closure of \(E\) but in the closure of no nonspanning subset of \(E\). If \(r=0\), the new element is a loop under this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free extension adds an element that can augment every nonspanning independent set but does not increase the matroid's total rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M+e)\setminus e=M\) and \(r(M+e)=r(M)\).

notation.meaning: free extension of M by e

source_refs.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

children.title: Quotient–Lift Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between quotient and lift constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient–Lift Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States deletion–contraction duality for quotient and lift relations on a common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) and \(N\) be finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\). Say that \(N\) is a quotient of \(M\) if there exist a finite set \(X\) disjoint from \(E\) and a matroid \(L\) on \(E\cup X\) such that \(M=L\setminus X\) and \(N=L/X\); equivalently, \(M\) is a lift of \(N\). Since duality interchanges deletion and contraction,
\[N\text{ is a quotient of }M\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N^*\text{ is a lift of }M^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality reverses the quotient relation: N is a quotient of M exactly when the dual of N is a lift of the dual of M.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(N\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is a quotient of \(M\) if and only if \(N^*\) is a lift of \(M^*\).

source_refs.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

children.title: Truncation–Free-Extension Relation
children.top_down_role: Structural connection between truncation and free-extension regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncation–Free-Extension Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents ordinary truncation as contraction of a freely added element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank \(r>0\), and let \(M+e\) be its free extension by an element \(e\notin E\). Then
\[(M+e)/e=T_{r-1}(M).\]
Equivalently, its rank function satisfies
\[r_{(M+e)/e}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),r-1\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
Thus every ordinary truncation of a positive-rank matroid has a free-extension-and-contraction representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freely adding one element to a positive-rank matroid and then contracting it produces the original matroid truncated by one rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank \(r>0\).

notation.meaning: free extension of M by e

source_refs.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

children.title: Matroid Class-Representation Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Class examples and representation regimes used by optimization, recognition, parity, and decomposition results.

children.title: Uniform Matroids
children.top_down_role: Cardinality-bounded canonical matroids.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite uniform matroid by a single global cardinality capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite set \(E\) of cardinality \(n\) and an integer \(r\) with \(0\le r\le n\), the uniform matroid \(U_{r,n}\) has independent sets
\[\mathcal I(U_{r,n})=\{I\subseteq E:|I|\le r\}.\]
Consequently every \(r\)-subset is a basis, every subset of size at most \(r\) is independent, and its rank function is
\[r_{U_{r,n}}(X)=\min\{|X|,r\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uniform matroid of rank r declares every subset of at most r elements independent and every larger subset dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(U_{r,n})=\{I\subseteq E:|I|\le r\}\).

notation.meaning: uniform matroid of rank r on n elements

children.title: Partition Matroids
children.top_down_role: Block-capacity matroids induced by a ground-set partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines partition matroids through disjoint block-capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=E_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_m\) be a partition of a finite set, and choose integer capacities \(0\le b_i\le |E_i|\). The associated partition matroid has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap E_i|\le b_i\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\]
Its rank function is
\[r(X)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\min\{|X\cap E_i|,b_i\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
Thus feasibility is determined independently within each block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition matroid permits at most a prescribed number of selected elements from each block of a partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is independent exactly when \(|I\cap E_i|\le b_i\) for every \(i\).

children.title: Laminar Matroids
children.top_down_role: Capacity matroids induced by a laminar set family.

knowledge_statements.title: Laminar Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite laminar matroids using capacities on nested-or-disjoint subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite and let \(\mathcal L\subseteq 2^E\) be laminar: for all \(A,B\in\mathcal L\), either \(A\subseteq B\), \(B\subseteq A\), or \(A\cap B=\varnothing\). Assign each \(A\in\mathcal L\) an integer capacity \(0\le b(A)\le |A|\). The laminar matroid determined by \((\mathcal L,b)\) has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap A|\le b(A)\text{ for every }A\in\mathcal L\}.\]
The laminar nesting condition is what guarantees the matroid exchange axiom for these simultaneous capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A laminar matroid imposes cardinality capacities on a family of subsets in which every two sets are nested or disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap A|\le b(A)\ \forall A\in\mathcal L\}\) is a matroid independence system.

children.title: Capacity-Class Specializations
children.top_down_role: Containment and specialization relationships among uniform, partition, and laminar classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Class Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the nesting of global, partition, and laminar capacity matroid classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite cardinality-capacity matroids admit the specialization chain
\[\{\text{uniform matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{partition matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{laminar matroids}\}.\]
Specifically, \(U_{r,n}\) is the partition matroid with the single block \(E\) and capacity \(r\). A partition matroid with blocks \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) and capacities \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\) is the laminar matroid with \(\mathcal L=\{E_1,\ldots,E_m\}\) and \(b(E_i)=b_i\). Adding nested sets to \(\mathcal L\) yields capacities shared across several descendant blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform matroids are one-block partition matroids, and partition matroids are laminar matroids whose constrained sets are pairwise disjoint.
assumptions_latex: All ground sets and capacity families are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{Uniform}\subseteq\mathrm{Partition}\subseteq\mathrm{Laminar}\).

notation.meaning: uniform matroid of rank r on n elements

children.title: Scheduling Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroid classes induced by schedulability constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the unit-time, single-machine deadline-feasibility version of a scheduling matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite set of unit-processing-time jobs, each with an integer deadline \(d_j\ge1\), to be scheduled without idle-time restrictions on one machine starting at time zero. Define
\[\mathcal I=\left\{I\subseteq E:\left|\{j\in I:d_j\le t\}\right|\le t\text{ for every integer }t\ge1\right\}.\]
Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid. Its independent sets are exactly the job subsets admitting an ordering in which every job completes no later than its deadline; earliest-deadline-first provides such an ordering whenever the inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit-time jobs with deadlines form a matroid: a subset is independent exactly when it can be scheduled on one machine without missing a deadline.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite collection of unit-time jobs.
Each deadline \(d_j\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is schedulable by its deadlines if and only if \(|\{j\in I:d_j\le t\}|\le t\) for all integers \(t\ge1\).

children.title: Count Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids governed by subset-count capacity constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Count Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard vertex-weighted graphical count-matroid construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless graph, let \(m:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and let \(\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) satisfy \(m(u)+m(v)\ge\ell+1\) for every edge \(uv\in E\). For \(F\subseteq E\), write \(V(F)\) for its incident vertices. The count matroid has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le m(V(F'))-\ell\text{ for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F\},\]
where \(m(X)=\sum_{v\in X}m(v)\). Under the stated edge condition, this system satisfies the matroid axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphical count matroid bounds every nonempty edge subset by the total weights of its incident vertices minus a fixed offset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I=\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le m(V(F'))-\ell\ \forall\varnothing\ne F'\subseteq F\}\) is a matroid independence system.

notation.meaning: vertices incident with edges of F
sum of vertex weights over X

children.title: Sparsity Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids arising from sparsity constraints on combinatorial structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite graphical sparsity matroids in the standard integer parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless graph, let \(k\ge1\), and let \(0\le\ell\le2k-1\) be integers. An edge set \(F\subseteq E\) is \((k,\ell)\)-sparse when every nonempty \(F'\subseteq F\) satisfies
\[|F'|\le k|V(F')|-\ell.\]
The family of all \((k,\ell)\)-sparse subsets of \(E\) is the independent-set family of the \((k,\ell)\)-sparsity matroid of \(G\). A spanning set is \((k,\ell)\)-tight when it is sparse and has \(|F|=k|V|-\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity matroid declares an edge set independent when every nonempty subcollection has at most k times its incident-vertex count minus l edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le k|V(F')|-\ell\ \forall\varnothing\ne F'\subseteq F\}\) is a matroid independence system.

source_refs.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: Section 5.4, Constructing matroids, p. 185

children.title: Constraint-Generation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating matroidal constraint systems from nonmatroidal ones.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Generation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that arbitrary overlapping cardinality constraints need not define a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=\{1,2,3\}\) and impose the two capacities
\[|I\cap\{1,2\}|\le1,\qquad |I\cap\{2,3\}|\le1.\]
The resulting hereditary family contains \(A=\{2\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\), with \(|A|<|B|\). However, neither \(A\cup\{1\}\) nor \(A\cup\{3\}\) is feasible. Hence the augmentation axiom fails, so arbitrary overlapping capacity sets do not necessarily generate a matroid. Structural hypotheses such as disjointness, laminarity, or an appropriate submodular count construction are therefore essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two crossing capacity constraints on three elements yield a hereditary system that violates augmentation, proving that arbitrary constraint families need not define matroids.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility means satisfying both displayed cardinality inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\{2\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\) violate matroid augmentation; therefore the feasible family is not a matroid.

children.title: Graphic Matroids
children.top_down_role: Cycle matroids arising from graphs.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph; loops and parallel edges are allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(G)=(E,\mathcal I_G)\) is the graphic, or cycle, matroid of \(G\).

notation.meaning: Family of edge sets containing no graph-theoretic cycle
Graphic matroid represented by the graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multigraph cycle-matroid definition, including loops and parallel edges.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I_G=\{F\subseteq E:(V,F)\text{ contains no cycle}\}\). Then \(\mathcal I_G\) is the independent-set family of a matroid \(M(G)\) on \(E\), called the graphic matroid of \(G\). Its circuits are precisely the edge sets of graph-theoretic cycles, including a loop as a one-element cycle and two parallel edges as a two-element cycle. Its bases are the maximal forests of \(G\); if \(G\) is connected, these are exactly its spanning trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphic matroid has graph edges as elements and forests as independent sets; its circuits are graph cycles and its bases are maximal forests.
knowledge_statements.title: Graphic Matroids

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vector, Representable, Graphic, and Uniform Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Introduces several standard matroid classes and notes that field representability is not universal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matrix $A$ over a field $F$, the matroid whose independent sets are the linearly independent subsets of columns of $A$ is the vector matroid of $A$. A matroid is representable over $F$ if it is the vector matroid of some matrix over $F$, and some matroids are not representable over any field. For a graph $G$, the matroid whose independent edge sets are forests is its cycle matroid $\mathcal M(G)$; a matroid is graphic if it is the cycle matroid of some graph, possibly with loops. Matroids with independent sets $\{X\subseteq E:|X|\le k\}$ are uniform matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column independence defines a vector matroid, and a matroid is representable over a field when it has such a matrix representation. Not every matroid is representable over a field. Forest edge sets define the cycle matroid of a graph; graphic matroids are cycle matroids of graphs, including graphs with loops. Cardinality-bounded independence systems are uniform matroids.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is a matrix over a field }F\text{ for the vector-matroid definition}
G\text{ is a graph, possibly with loops, for the graphic-matroid definition}
E\text{ is finite and }k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\text{ for the uniform-matroid family}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is representable over }F\iff \mathcal M\text{ is the vector matroid of a matrix over }F;\quad \exists\mathcal M\ \forall F,\ \mathcal M\text{ is not representable over }F,\quad\text{with graphic and uniform matroids defined as stated.}

children.title: Cographic Matroids
children.top_down_role: Bond matroids arising as duals of graphic matroids.

assumptions_latex: \(M(G)^*\) denotes the matroid dual of the graphic matroid of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cographic matroid of \(G\) is \(M^*(G)=M(G)^*\), whose circuits are the bonds of \(G\).

notation.meaning: Cographic or bond matroid of the graph
Number of connected components of the indicated graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite cographic matroids defined by dualizing cycle matroids.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53
Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cographic matroid of \(G\), also called its bond matroid, is \(M^*(G):=M(G)^*\). Thus \(B\subseteq E\) is a basis of \(M^*(G)\) exactly when \(E\setminus B\) is a maximal forest of \(G\). The circuits of \(M^*(G)\) are precisely the bonds: the inclusion-minimal nonempty edge cuts whose deletion increases \(c(G)\). Consequently, \(X\subseteq E\) is independent in \(M^*(G)\) exactly when \(X\) contains no bond of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cographic matroid is the dual of a graph's cycle matroid. Its circuits are the graph's inclusion-minimal nonempty edge cuts, called bonds.
knowledge_statements.title: Cographic Matroids

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53
Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Bicircular Matroids
children.top_down_role: Graph-derived matroids governed by pseudoforest structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pseudoforests of \(G\) form the independent sets of the bicircular matroid \(B(G)\).

notation.meaning: Bicircular matroid represented by the graph
Number of vertices incident with edges of the subgraph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite bicircular matroid in its pseudoforest formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I_B=\{F\subseteq E:\text{every connected component of }(V,F)\text{ contains at most one cycle}\}\). Equivalently, \(F\in\mathcal I_B\) if and only if every nonempty subgraph \(H\) of \((V,F)\) satisfies \(|E(H)|\le |V(H)|\). The family \(\mathcal I_B\) is the independent-set family of a matroid on \(E\), called the bicircular matroid \(B(G)\). Its circuits are the inclusion-minimal edge sets inducing a connected subgraph with two cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bicircular matroid has graph edges as elements and pseudoforests, whose components each contain at most one cycle, as independent sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Bicircular Matroids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pseudoforest formulation is standard, but no source supports the specialized definition or the circuit characterization. A source should also state the latter using minimal failure of the pseudoforest condition or cyclomatic number two, avoiding ambiguity in “two cycles.”

children.title: Frame Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids represented through biased-graph frame structure.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is a frame matroid exactly when it possesses a basis \(B\) satisfying the stated two-element spanning condition.

notation.meaning: A distinguished basis witnessing the frame property

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-matroid definition using a framing basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(M\) is a frame matroid if there exists a basis \(B\) of \(M\) such that, for every \(e\in E\), some subset \(X_e\subseteq B\) with \(|X_e|\le 2\) satisfies \(e\in\operatorname{cl}_M(X_e)\). Equivalently, after deleting loops, every element \(e\in E\setminus B\) has a fundamental circuit \(C(e,B)\) with \(|C(e,B)|\le 3\). Such a basis \(B\) is called a frame for \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A frame matroid has a basis such that every element is spanned by at most two basis elements; equivalently, each fundamental circuit has at most three elements.
knowledge_statements.title: Frame Matroids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The framing-basis condition and fundamental-circuit equivalence are mathematically plausible and fit the leaf, but frame-matroid conventions vary and no exact source is supplied.

children.title: Graphic–Cographic Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual relationship between cycle and bond matroids.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite connected plane graph and \(G^*\) is its geometric dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(G)^*=M(G^*)\) under the natural edge correspondence.

notation.meaning: Cycle matroid of the plane graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Plane-graph form of graphic-cographic duality.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53
0.2 Graph Theory p. 16

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Identify each edge \(e\in E(G)\) with the dual edge \(e^*\in E(G^*)\). For every \(B\subseteq E(G)\), \(B\) is a spanning-tree edge set of \(G\) if and only if \(\{e^*:e\in E(G)\setminus B\}\) is a spanning-tree edge set of \(G^*\). Hence the bases of \(M(G)^*\) and \(M(G^*)\) coincide under this correspondence, so \(M(G)^*=M(G^*)\). Thus every planar graphic matroid has a graphic dual, represented by a plane dual graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a connected plane graph, complements of spanning trees correspond to spanning trees of the geometric dual, so the dual cycle matroid is again graphic.
knowledge_statements.title: Graphic–Cographic Duality

children.title: Graph-Derived Class Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Containment and separation among the principal graph-derived matroid classes.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the multigraph with two vertices joined by four parallel edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(G)\cong U_{2,4}\), while \(U_{2,4}\) is neither graphic nor cographic.

notation.meaning: Bicircular matroid represented by the graph
Uniform rank-two matroid on four elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation of bicircular matroids from graphic and cographic classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every edge subset of \(G\) having at most two elements induces at most one cycle, whereas every three-edge subset induces two cycles. Therefore \(B(G)\cong U_{2,4}\). The matroid \(U_{2,4}\) is not representable over \(\mathbb F_2\), since a rank-two binary vector space has only three nonzero one-dimensional subspaces. Every graphic and every cographic matroid is binary. Consequently, \(B(G)\) is neither graphic nor cographic, so graph-derived matroid constructions do not define a single matroid class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four parallel edges yield the bicircular matroid U(2,4), which is nonbinary and therefore neither graphic nor cographic, separating these graph-derived classes.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Derived Class Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-parallel-edge construction does yield the nonbinary matroid U_{2,4}, separating bicircular matroids from graphic and cographic matroids, but none of the nontrivial class-boundary claims has a cited source.

assumptions_latex: \(A=(A_j)_{j\in J}\) is a finite family of subsets of a finite set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partial transversals of \(A\) form the independent sets of the transversal matroid \(M[A]\).

notation.meaning: Transversal matroid presented by the set family
Index set of the presenting family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite set-system definition via partial systems of distinct representatives.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(I\subseteq X\) is a partial transversal of \(A\) if there exist an injection \(\phi:I\to J\) such that \(x\in A_{\phi(x)}\) for every \(x\in I\). Equivalently, in the bipartite graph with parts \(X\) and \(J\), where \(xj\) is an edge exactly when \(x\in A_j\), the vertices of \(I\) can be matched into \(J\). The family of all partial transversals is the independent-set family of a matroid on \(X\), denoted \(M[A]\) and called a transversal matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transversal matroid is presented by a set family; its independent sets are elements that can be assigned injectively to containing sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Transversal Matroids

children.title: Strict Gammoids
children.top_down_role: Linkage matroids presented directly from directed graphs with designated sinks.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed graph and \(T\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linkable subsets of \(V\) form the strict gammoid \(L(D,T)\).

notation.meaning: Strict gammoid presented by a directed graph and target set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite strict gammoid with the entire vertex set as ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(I\subseteq V\) is linkable to \(T\) if there exist \(|I|\) pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths in \(D\), each beginning at a distinct vertex of \(I\) and ending at a distinct vertex of \(T\); paths of length zero are permitted. The family \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq V:I\text{ is linkable to }T\}\) is the independent-set family of a matroid on the full vertex set \(V\). This matroid is the strict gammoid \(L(D,T)\) presented by \((D,T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict gammoid uses all vertices of a directed graph as its ground set; independent sets can be linked disjointly to designated targets.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Gammoids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated full-vertex-set linkage definition is a standard strict-gammoid convention, but path orientation, zero-length paths, and endpoint conventions require an exact source.

children.title: General Gammoids
children.top_down_role: The broader linkage class obtained through restrictions of strict gammoids.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed graph, \(T\subseteq V\), and \(S\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linkable subsets of \(S\) form the gammoid \(L(D,T)|S\).

notation.meaning: Strict gammoid on the full vertex set
Restriction to the chosen ground set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite gammoid represented on a chosen subset of the digraph vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(I\subseteq S\) is independent when it is linkable to \(T\) by pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths in \(D\), with distinct initial vertices in \(I\) and distinct terminal vertices in \(T\). These independent sets define the matroid \(L(D,T)|S\), the restriction to \(S\) of the strict gammoid \(L(D,T)\) on \(V\). A finite matroid is a gammoid if it is isomorphic to \(L(D,T)|S\) for some finite \(D\), target set \(T\), and ground subset \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general gammoid restricts a strict gammoid to selected vertices; independence still means linkability by vertex-disjoint directed paths to designated targets.
knowledge_statements.title: General Gammoids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restriction-of-a-strict-gammoid formulation fits General Gammoids and is internally consistent, but no source verifies the directed-linkage convention or the class definition.

children.title: Strict-to-General Gammoid Passage
children.top_down_role: Structural passage from strict gammoids to the full gammoid class.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is a deletion minor of the strict gammoid \(L(D,T)\).

notation.meaning: Strict gammoid on all vertices of the presentation digraph
Deletion of elements outside the selected ground set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction, equivalently deletion-minor, passage from strict gammoids to gammoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The strict gammoid \(N:=L(D,T)\) has ground set \(V\). Restricting its independent sets to subsets of \(S\) preserves exactly those subsets of \(S\) that are linkable to \(T\) in \(D\). Hence \[M=N|S=N\backslash(V\setminus S).\] Therefore every gammoid is a restriction, and thus a deletion minor, of a strict gammoid. Conversely, every restriction of a strict gammoid is a gammoid by the same directed-linkage presentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every gammoid is obtained by restricting a strict gammoid to selected vertices, equivalently by deleting the other vertices; every such restriction is a gammoid.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-to-General Gammoid Passage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restriction/deletion identity is correct given the preceding definition and the representation content kind fits this passage leaf, but the strict-to-general characterization has no cited support.

children.title: Gammoid Representation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of directed-linkage presentations for matroid classes.

assumptions_latex: \(D\) has four source vertices \(S=\{s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4\}\), two targets \(T=\{t_1,t_2\}\), and every arc \(s_i t_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(D,T)|S\cong U_{2,4}\), a gammoid not representable over \(\mathbb F_2\).

notation.meaning: Uniform rank-two matroid on four elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that gammoid status does not imply binary representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(I\subseteq S\) links to \(T\) exactly when \(|I|\le 2\), because each source reaches either target directly and the paths must have distinct endpoints. Thus \(L(D,T)|S\cong U_{2,4}\). If \(U_{2,4}\) had a rank-two representation over \(\mathbb F_2\), its four nonparallel elements would require four distinct one-dimensional subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^2\), but only three exist. Hence this gammoid is not binary. Directed-linkage representability therefore does not imply representability over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete four-source, two-target linkage presentation gives U(2,4), a gammoid that is not binary, so gammoid representation does not ensure every-field linear representability.
knowledge_statements.title: Gammoid Representation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linkage construction yields U_{2,4}, and its nonrepresentability over F_2 is correctly stated, but the boundary record lacks a source for the gammoid presentation and representability claim.

children.title: Matrix Representations
children.top_down_role: Linear presentations of matroids by column-dependence data.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(\mathbb F\) is a field.
\(A\) is a matrix over \(\mathbb F\) whose columns are indexed by \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) represents \(M\) over \(\mathbb F\) exactly when matroid independence equals column independence.

notation.meaning: Submatrix formed by columns indexed by a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroid representation by columns over a fixed field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matrix \(A\) represents \(M\) over \(\mathbb F\) if, for every \(X\subseteq E\), \[X\text{ is independent in }M\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}A[X]=|X|.\] Equivalently, the column matroid \(M[A]\) equals \(M\). Under this correspondence, matroid circuits are the inclusion-minimal linearly dependent column sets, bases are column bases, and \(r_M(X)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}A[X]\) for every \(X\subseteq E\). A matroid admitting such a matrix is representable over \(\mathbb F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix represents a matroid when each element labels a column and matroid-independent sets are exactly the linearly independent column sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Representations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Projective Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence of matrix presentations under projective transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb F\) is a field and \(E\) is a finite labeled set.
\(A,B\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\) have full row rank and represent matroids on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}B\iff (\exists P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F))(\exists D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\text{ invertible diagonal})\;B=PAD\).

notation.meaning: projective equivalence over the fixed field with labeled columns
group of invertible rank-by-rank matrices over the field

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses labeled ground sets and excludes field automorphisms from projective equivalence.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be full-row-rank matrices over \(\mathbb F\), with columns indexed by the same labeled set \(E\). They are projectively equivalent if there exist an invertible matrix \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F)\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\) such that \(B=PAD\). Thus projective equivalence permits elementary changes of coordinates in the ambient vector space and independent nonzero rescaling of columns, while preserving column labels. Projectively equivalent matrices represent the same matroid on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labeled matrix representations are projectively equivalent when one is obtained from the other by invertible row operations and independent nonzero column scalings.
knowledge_statements.title: Projective Equivalence

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Representation Equivalence Classes
children.top_down_role: Organization of matrix presentations into structural equivalence classes.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a rank-\(r\) matroid on a finite labeled set \(E\), representable over a field \(\mathbb F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}=\{[A]_{\mathrm{proj}}:A\in\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)\}\).

notation.meaning: full-row-rank labeled matrices over the field representing the matroid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The quotient is taken among full-row-rank representations with the ground-set labels fixed.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \(\mathbb F\)-representable matroid \(M\) of rank \(r\) on labeled ground set \(E\), let \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)\) be the set of full-row-rank matrices in \(\mathbb F^{r\times E}\) whose column matroid is \(M\). Projective equivalence restricts to an equivalence relation on this set. Its equivalence classes are \([A]_{\mathrm{proj}}=\{PAD:P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F),\ D\text{ invertible diagonal}\}\), intersected with \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)\). The representation-equivalence space is the quotient \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representations of a fixed labeled matroid split into classes under invertible row transformations and nonzero column scalings.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence Classes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Representation Uniqueness
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which a matroid has a unique projective representation.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid representable over a fixed field \(\mathbb F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is uniquely representable over }\mathbb F\iff \left|\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}\right|=1\).

notation.meaning: the set of projective-equivalence classes of labeled field representations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness is over one fixed field and for a fixed labeling of the ground set.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M\) on a fixed labeled ground set \(E\) is uniquely representable over \(\mathbb F\) if it is \(\mathbb F\)-representable and any two full-row-rank \(\mathbb F\)-matrices \(A\) and \(B\) representing \(M\) are projectively equivalent. Equivalently, for every such pair there are \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_{r(M)}(\mathbb F)\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\) satisfying \(B=PAD\). Hence unique representability is exactly the condition that \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}\) has one element.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is uniquely representable over a fixed field when all its labeled representations belong to one projective-equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Uniqueness

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\) has full row rank and represents a matroid \(M\).
\(B\in\mathbb F^{(|E|-r)\times E}\) has row space \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AB^{\mathsf T}=0\quad\text{and}\quad M(B)=M(A)^*=M^*\).

notation.meaning: column matroid represented by a matrix
nullspace of the linear map defined by the matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dual construction over an arbitrary fixed field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\) have full row rank and column matroid \(M\). Choose a matrix \(B\in\mathbb F^{(|E|-r)\times E}\) whose rows form a basis of \(\ker A\), so \(AB^{\mathsf T}=0\). Then the column matroid of \(B\) is the dual matroid \(M^*\). Explicitly, for every \(X\subseteq E\), the set \(X\) is a basis of \(M(B)\) exactly when \(E\setminus X\) is a basis of \(M(A)\). Different choices of a row basis for \(\ker A\) give projectively equivalent dual representations up to permitted column scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix whose row space is the nullspace of a representation matrix represents the dual matroid on the same labeled ground set.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Linear Representations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Binary Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids representable over the binary field.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is binary}\iff (\exists A\in\mathbb F_2^{r(M)\times E})\;M=M(A)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-matroid definition by matrix representability over the two-element field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite matroid \(M\) of rank \(r(M)\) on ground set \(E\) is binary if there exists a matrix \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{r(M)\times E}\) such that a subset \(I\subseteq E\) is independent in \(M\) exactly when the columns of \(A\) indexed by \(I\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb F_2\). Equivalently, \(M=M(A)\) for some matrix over the two-element field. Loops correspond to zero columns, and parallel nonloops correspond to equal nonzero columns in a binary representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary matroid is a finite matroid representable by a matrix over the two-element field.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary Matroids

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Ternary Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids representable over the ternary field.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is ternary}\iff (\exists A\in\mathbb F_3^{r(M)\times E})\;M=M(A)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-matroid definition by matrix representability over the three-element field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite matroid \(M\) of rank \(r(M)\) on ground set \(E\) is ternary if there exists a matrix \(A\in\mathbb F_3^{r(M)\times E}\) such that a subset \(I\subseteq E\) is independent in \(M\) exactly when the columns indexed by \(I\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb F_3\). Equivalently, \(M=M(A)\) for some matrix over the three-element field. This definition fixes the field itself, not merely its characteristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ternary matroid is a finite matroid representable by a matrix over the three-element field.
knowledge_statements.title: Ternary Matroids

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Regular Matroids
children.top_down_role: Matroids representable over every field.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines regularity through universal field representability; equivalent matrix characterizations are omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite matroid \(M\) is regular if, for every field \(\mathbb F\), there exists a matrix over \(\mathbb F\) whose column-dependence matroid is \(M\). The representing matrix may depend on \(\mathbb F\), while the represented independent-set system remains \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular matroid is representable over every field, although its representing matrix may vary with the field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is regular}\iff (\forall\text{ fields }\mathbb F)\;M\text{ is representable over }\mathbb F\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Binary–Ternary Intersection
children.top_down_role: Structural overlap between binary and ternary representability.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary–Ternary Intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid binary–ternary characterization of regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite matroid \(M\), the following are equivalent: \(M\) is regular; and \(M\) is representable over both \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\). Equivalently, the intersection of the class of binary matroids and the class of ternary matroids is the class of regular matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite matroid is regular exactly when it is representable over both the two-element and three-element fields.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is regular}\iff M\text{ is binary and ternary}\).

notation.meaning: the fields with two and three elements

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Field-Regime Separation
children.top_down_role: Class boundaries separating binary, ternary, and regular representability.

knowledge_statements.title: Field-Regime Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A minimal example separating binary and larger-field representability regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every field \(\mathbb F\), the uniform matroid \(U_{2,4}\) is representable over \(\mathbb F\) if and only if \(|\mathbb F|\ge 3\). In particular, \(U_{2,4}\) is ternary but not binary, demonstrating that representability depends on the chosen field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matroid U(2,4) is representable over a field exactly when the field has at least three elements; in particular, it is ternary but not binary.
assumptions_latex: \(U_{2,4}\) denotes the rank-two uniform matroid on four elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_{2,4}\text{ is representable over }\mathbb F\iff |\mathbb F|\ge 3\).

notation.meaning: rank-two uniform matroid on four elements

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Fixed-Field Representability
children.top_down_role: Representability of matroids over a specified finite field.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a finite matroid and \(\mathbb F\) is a fixed field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff (\exists A\in\mathbb F^{r(M)\times E})(\forall I\subseteq E)\;[I\in\mathcal I\iff A[I]\text{ has independent columns}]\).

notation.meaning: submatrix consisting of columns indexed by the set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability is relative to one specified field, with columns indexed by the ground set.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is representable over a fixed field \(\mathbb F\) if there exists a matrix \(A\in\mathbb F^{r(M)\times E}\), with columns labeled by \(E\), such that for every subset \(I\subseteq E\), one has \(I\in\mathcal I\) exactly when the columns of \(A[I]\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb F\). Zero columns represent loops, and proportional nonzero columns represent parallel elements. The field is part of the predicate: representability over another field is a distinct condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is representable over a fixed field when its independent sets are exactly the linearly independent column sets of a matrix over that field.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Field Representability

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Excluded-Minor Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Minor-minimal barriers to representability over a fixed finite field.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\in\mathcal X_{\mathbb F}\iff N\notin\mathcal R_{\mathbb F}\text{ and every proper minor of }N\text{ lies in }\mathcal R_{\mathbb F}\).

notation.meaning: class of finite matroids representable over the fixed field
class of excluded minors for fixed-field representability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines excluded minors without asserting finiteness of the obstruction set.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathbb F}\) be the class of finite matroids representable over \(\mathbb F\). A finite matroid \(N\) is an excluded minor for \(\mathbb F\)-representability if \(N\notin\mathcal R_{\mathbb F}\) but every proper minor of \(N\), obtained by at least one deletion or contraction, belongs to \(\mathcal R_{\mathbb F}\). Writing the set of these minimal obstructions as \(\mathcal X_{\mathbb F}\), a finite matroid \(M\) is \(\mathbb F\)-representable exactly when no minor of \(M\) is isomorphic to a member of \(\mathcal X_{\mathbb F}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An excluded minor is minimally nonrepresentable over the fixed field: it fails representability while every proper minor satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.title: Excluded-Minor Obstructions

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Field-Size Dependence
children.top_down_role: Variation of representability behavior with finite-field size.

knowledge_statements.title: Field-Size Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp finite-field size boundary supplied by rank-two uniform matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every prime power \(q\) and integer \(n\ge 2\), the rank-two uniform matroid \(U_{2,n}\) is representable over \(\mathbb F_q\) if and only if \(n\le q+1\). Thus \(U_{2,q+1}\) is representable over \(\mathbb F_q\), whereas \(U_{2,q+2}\) is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-two uniform matroid on n elements is representable over the q-element field exactly when n is at most q+1.
assumptions_latex: \(U_{2,n}\) is the rank-two uniform matroid on \(n\) elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_{2,n}\text{ is representable over }\mathbb F_q\iff n\le q+1\).

notation.meaning: rank-two uniform matroid on n elements

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Characteristic Dependence
children.top_down_role: Variation of representability behavior with field characteristic.

assumptions_latex: Representability is by finite matrices over fields, with the column-dependence matroid convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Char}(M)\) can depend essentially on field characteristic; specifically, \(\operatorname{Char}(F_7)=\{2\}\) and \(\operatorname{Char}(F_7^-)=\{0\}\cup\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\ne2\}\).

notation.meaning: Set of field characteristics over which M is representable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid representability over arbitrary fields, including characteristic zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M\), define \(\operatorname{Char}(M)=\{\operatorname{char}(K):K\text{ is a field over which }M\text{ is representable}\}\), where characteristic zero is recorded as \(0\). Representability is not determined solely by rank or ground-set size and may depend sharply on characteristic. The Fano matroid satisfies \(\operatorname{Char}(F_7)=\{2\}\), whereas its relaxation, the non-Fano matroid, satisfies \(\operatorname{Char}(F_7^-)=\{0\}\cup\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\ne2\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid may be representable only in selected characteristics: the Fano matroid requires characteristic two, while the non-Fano matroid requires characteristic different from two.
knowledge_statements.title: Characteristic Dependence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The characteristic claims are mathematically standard and the property kind fits the leaf, but no citation supports the exact Fano and non-Fano assertions.

children.title: Projective Geometries
children.top_down_role: Matroid geometries arising from finite projective spaces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting simple rank-\(r\) matroid is the projective geometry \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\).

notation.meaning: Projective geometry matroid of rank r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite projective geometries viewed as simple linear matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\mathbb F_q^r\). The ground set of \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) is the set of one-dimensional linear subspaces of \(V\). Choose one nonzero vector from each such subspace. A set of projective points is independent exactly when the corresponding chosen vectors are linearly independent over \(\mathbb F_q\); this condition is independent of the choices because replacing a representative by a nonzero scalar multiple preserves linear dependence. Thus \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) is a simple rank-\(r\) matroid with \((q^r-1)/(q-1)\) elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projective geometry is the simple linear matroid whose elements are one-dimensional subspaces of a finite vector space.
knowledge_statements.title: Projective Geometries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind appear correct, but the record supplies no inspectable citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Affine Geometries
children.top_down_role: Matroid geometries arising from finite affine spaces.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The column matroid of \(A\) is the rank-\(r\) affine geometry \(\operatorname{AG}(r-1,q)\).

notation.meaning: Affine geometry matroid of rank r
Matrix with one column for every affine point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite affine geometries in their homogeneous-coordinate representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the \(r\times q^{r-1}\) matrix \(A\) over \(\mathbb F_q\) whose columns are all vectors \((1,x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})^{\mathsf T}\) with \((x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})\in\mathbb F_q^{r-1}\). The affine geometry \(\operatorname{AG}(r-1,q)\) is the column-dependence matroid of \(A\). Equivalently, its points are the elements of the affine space \(\mathbb F_q^{r-1}\), and a subset is matroid-independent exactly when its homogeneous-coordinate columns are linearly independent. It is a simple rank-\(r\) matroid on \(q^{r-1}\) elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine geometry is represented by homogeneous coordinate columns whose first coordinate is one and whose remaining coordinates range over a finite field.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Geometries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The homogeneous-coordinate definition appears correct and fits the leaf, but it has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Dowling Geometries
children.top_down_role: Group-labeled geometric matroid families extending graphic structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The frame matroid of the complete \(G\)-gain graph with joints is the rank-\(n\) Dowling geometry \(Q_n(G)\).

notation.meaning: Dowling geometry of rank n associated with G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial definition through complete gain graphs and frame matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take vertices \(1,ldots,n\), one distinguished unbalanced loop at each vertex, and, for every \(i<j\) and \(g\in G\), an edge \(e_{ij}^g\) directed from \(i\) to \(j\). Reversing an edge inverts its gain, and a cycle is balanced when its directed gain product equals \(1_G\). The Dowling geometry \(Q_n(G)\) is the frame matroid of this biased graph: an edge set is independent exactly when it contains no balanced cycle and every connected component contains at most one cycle. The distinguished loops are the joints of the geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Dowling geometry is the frame matroid of a complete group-labeled graph augmented by one unbalanced joint at each vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Dowling Geometries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The specialized gain-graph convention requires authoritative support. The statement also contains the malformed vertex text "1,ldots,n" and includes explanatory justification unsuitable for a proof-free knowledge statement.

children.title: Projective–Affine Passage
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between projective geometries and affine restrictions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\backslash H\cong\operatorname{AG}(r-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hyperplane deletion identifies finite projective and affine geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose homogeneous coordinates on \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) so that \(H\) consists of the points satisfying \(x_0=0\). Every point outside \(H\) has a unique representative whose first coordinate is \(1\), hence has the form \((1,x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})^{\mathsf T}\) with \((x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})\in\mathbb F_q^{r-1}\). Under this normalization, the restriction of the projective-geometry matroid to the complement of \(H\) is the affine-geometry matroid. Therefore \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\backslash H\cong\operatorname{AG}(r-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a hyperplane from a finite projective geometry leaves the corresponding affine geometry, represented by normalizing the first homogeneous coordinate to one.
knowledge_statements.title: Projective–Affine Passage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projective–affine identification and representation kind fit the leaf, but no citation is supplied, and the coordinate derivation is proof-style text.

children.title: Geometric Specialization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Specialization and separation among projective, affine, and Dowling families.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite simple matroid of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is representable over \(\mathbb F_q\) if and only if \(M\) is isomorphic to a restriction of \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\).

notation.meaning: Restriction of a matroid to X
Rank-r projective geometry over the q-element field

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simple finite-field representable matroids as projective-geometry restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The following conditions are equivalent: \(M\) is representable over \(\mathbb F_q\); and there exists a subset \(X\) of the points of \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) such that \(M\cong\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)|X\). Indeed, in any full-rank \(\mathbb F_q\)-matrix representing a simple matroid, no column is zero and no two columns are scalar multiples, so its columns determine distinct projective points. Conversely, choosing representatives of any set of projective points yields an \(\mathbb F_q\)-matrix for the corresponding restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple rank-r matroid is representable over a finite field exactly when it is a restriction of that field's rank-r projective geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Specialization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restriction characterization is correctly scoped to finite simple rank-r matroids and theorem is the proper kind, but it lacks a source and includes an explicit proof beginning with "Indeed".

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite and \(x_e\in L\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algebraically independent subsets form a matroid, with rank \(\operatorname{trdeg}_K K(x_e:e\in E)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite algebraic matroids induced by elements of a field extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:\{x_e:e\in I\}\text{ is algebraically independent over }K\}\). Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is the algebraic matroid of the family \((x_e)_{e\in E}\) over \(K\). Its rank function is \(r(S)=\operatorname{trdeg}_K K(x_e:e\in S)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\). Consequently, a set is dependent precisely when its indexed elements satisfy a nonzero polynomial relation with coefficients in \(K\). A finite matroid is algebraic over \(K\) if it is isomorphic to one obtained in this way.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An algebraic matroid records algebraic independence among finitely many elements of a field extension; its rank is transcendence degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Matroids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic-matroid definition and transcendence-degree rank formula appear correct, but no inspectable citation is provided.

children.title: Partial-Field Representations
children.top_down_role: Matroid representations coordinated through partial-field structure.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb P=(R,G)\) is a partial field, where \(G\le R^\times\) contains \(-1\).
\(M\) is a finite matroid with a chosen basis \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([I_B\mid A]\) represents \(M\) over \(\mathbb P\) exactly when its nonzero maximal minors encode the bases of \(M\).

notation.meaning: Partial field with underlying set G union zero
Identity block indexed by the basis B
Nonbasis block of a representation matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix representations over partial fields using the standard determinant convention.
